STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white, square-ish flat plate with a raised rim band and a flat centre. No deep inner wall is visible, so it is a flat plate (square).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: a square dinner plate is 20-30 cm. The plate here looks like a medium-large square plate, roughly 25 cm.
b) Reference: the strawberries are about 3-4 cm long and the grapes about 2.2 cm. The plate spans about 10-11 strawberry lengths across (~3 cm each in the photo, roughly 30 cm width if strawberry ~3 cm, but the plate looks smaller relative to the food). Taking the plate width across the food area as about 8 strawberry-widths of ~3.2 cm gives ~26 cm.
Reconciled width: about 26 cm (square, area ~676 cm²).

STEP 3 - Items:
- Cottage/ricotta-style cheese (white curds): covers roughly 35% of the plate, about 236 cm². It is a mound, averaging about 2 cm thick. Volume = 236 x 2 = 472 ml x 1.0 = about 470 g.
- Sweet potato cubes (roasted): about 10% of the plate, about 68 cm², average 1.5 cm thick = 100 ml x 0.6 = about 60 g.
- Strawberries: 3 whole halves/slices, about 45 g total.
- Grapes (dark): about 5 grapes at 5 g each, plus one hidden = about 30 g.
- Melon/cantaloupe pieces (orange and green): about 8% of the plate, about 54 cm² x 1.5 cm = 81 ml x 0.6 = about 50 g; honeydew-type green melon pieces are included in this group, split roughly evenly, so I list them together as one item.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No clear base layer; the cheese is a mound with no visible sauce. No additional hidden items are counted.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g:
- Cottage/ricotta-style cheese: about 100 kcal/100 g (low-fat cottage cheese runs about 80-100; ricotta is about 170). Using 100.
- Roasted sweet potato: about 90 kcal/100 g.
- Strawberries: about 32 kcal/100 g.
- Grapes: about 69 kcal/100 g.
- Melon: about 34 kcal/100 g.

Totals: about 610 g, roughly 0.6 kg, which is in line with a heaped plate.
